<context>
You are an expert at solving ARC-AGI (Abstraction and Reasoning Corpus) puzzles using Answer Set Programming (ASP).

ARC-AGI puzzles show input-output grid transformations. Each cell contains a color value (integer 0–9). The goal is to discover the hidden transformation rule from training examples and encode it as an ASP program.
</context>

<rules>
- `input(row, col, color)` facts are injected automatically — do not define them.
- `color(0..9)` facts are injected automatically — do not define them.
- the output predicate is always `output(row, col, color)` — do not redefine it.
- the final program must produce exactly one answer set, in which `output(row, col, color)` match the expected output exactly.
- end your program with `#show output/3.`
</rules>

<example_1>
This puzzle copies the input to the output unchanged.

<grid_1>
Input:
<diagram>
0 1 0
2 0 3
0 4 0
</diagram>

Output:
<diagram>
0 1 0
2 0 3
0 4 0
</diagram>
</grid_1>

<asp>
% Grid dimensions
n_rows(N) :- N = #count{ R : input(R, _, _) }.
n_cols(N) :- N = #count{ C : input(_, C, _) }.
row(0..N-1) :- n_rows(N).
col(0..M-1) :- n_cols(M).

% Output has the same dimensions as the input
output_cell(R, C) :- row(R), col(C).

% Each output cell gets exactly one color
1 { output(R, C, Color) : color(Color) } 1 :- output_cell(R, C).

% Copy each input cell to the output unchanged
output(R, C, Color) :- input(R, C, Color).

#show output/3.
</asp>
</example_1>

<example_2>
This puzzle replaces every non-zero cell with color 5; zero cells stay 0.

<grid_1>
Input:
<diagram>
0 1 0
2 0 3
0 4 0
</diagram>

Output:
<diagram>
0 5 0
5 0 5
0 5 0
</diagram>
</grid_1>

<asp>
% Grid dimensions
n_rows(N) :- N = #count{ R : input(R, _, _) }.
n_cols(N) :- N = #count{ C : input(_, C, _) }.
row(0..N-1) :- n_rows(N).
col(0..M-1) :- n_cols(M).

% Output has the same dimensions as the input
output_cell(R, C) :- row(R), col(C).

% Each output cell gets exactly one color
1 { output(R, C, Color) : color(Color) } 1 :- output_cell(R, C).

% Recolor every non-zero cell to 5; zeros stay 0.
output(R, C, 5) :- input(R, C, V), V != 0.
output(R, C, 0) :- input(R, C, 0).

#show output/3.
</asp>
</example_2>

<example_3>

</diagram>

<asp>
% Grid dimensions
n_rows(N) :- N = #count{ R : input(R, _, _) }.
n_cols(N) :- N = #count{ C : input(_, C, _) }.
row(0..N-1) :- n_rows(N).
col(0..M-1) :- n_cols(M).

% Output has the same dimensions as the input
output_cell(R, C) :- row(R), col(C).

% Each output cell gets exactly one color
1 { output(R, C, Color) : color(Color) } 1 :- output_cell(R, C).

% Mirror: column C of the output is column (M-1-C) of the input.
output(R, C, Color) :- input(R, Cin, Color), n_cols(M), C = M - 1 - Cin.

#show output/3.
</asp>
</example_3>

nearest_left(R,C,ClCol,Cl) :- input(R,ClCol,Cl), Cl != 0, ClCol < C,
    not exists Cl2 : input(R,Cl2,_), Cl2 < C, Cl2 > ClCol.

% Nearest non‑zero to the right of a cell (its column and colour)
nearest_right(R,C,CrCol,Cr) :- input(R,CrCol,Cr), Cr != 0, CrCol > C,
    not exists Cr2 : input(R,Cr2,_), Cr2 > CrCol, Cr2 < C.

% Cells that are inside the shape (opposite colours on opposite sides
% and the distance to the opposite colour is smaller)
interior8(R,C) :- input(R,C,0),
    nearest_left(R,C,ClCol,8),
    nearest_right(R,C,CrCol,2),
    (C - ClCol) > (CrCol - C).

interior2(R,C) :- input(R,C,0),
    nearest_left(R,C,ClCol,2),
    nearest_right(R,C,CrCol,8),
    (C - ClCol) > (CrCol - C).

interior(R,C) :- interior8(R,C).
interior(R,C) :- interior2(R,C).

n_rows(N) :- N = #count{R : input(R,_,_)}.

right_wall(R) :- input(R,M-1,Cl), Cl != 0.

end_row(ER)   :- opening_row(ER),   not (exists R2 : opening_row(R2), R2 > ER).

% Rows strictly between start and end are interior rows

    (input(R,C,0), C > 0, input(R,C-1,Cl2), Cl2 != 0) ;
    (input(R,C,0), C < M-1, input(R,C+1,Cl2), Cl2 != 0).

    (input(R,C,0), C > 0, input(R,C-1,Cl2), Cl2 != 0) ;
    (input(R,C,0), C < M-1, input(R,C+1,Cl2), Cl2 != 0).

% The rightmost column that may become 3

    nearest_right(R,C,CrCol,8),
    (C - ClCol) > (CrCol - C).

interior(R,C) :- interior8(R,C).
interior(R,C) :- interior2(R,C).

% Constraints
% non‑zero cells keep original colour
:- output(R,C,X), input(R,C,Cl), Cl != 0, X != Cl.

% interior cells must be colour 3
:- output(R,C,X), interior(R,C), input(R,C,0), X != 3.

% other zero cells must stay 0
:- output(R,C,X), not interior(R,C), input(R,C,0), X != 0.

#show output/3.
